new_statements.rule_in_words: Non-tonal prominence (force + duration, often vowel lengthening) falls on the penultimate syllable before a pause, i.e. of the pre-pausal word/phrase; enclitics such as easterly /-nyi/ count as part of the word and shift the accent one syllable rightward (kuita ba:sa vs. basa:nyi). Tone (H/L) is lexically/grammatically contrastive and independent of this accent. Kagaya 2000 p.154 independently states for Manyika verbs in isolation that the penultimate syllable is lengthened to two morae.
new_statements.exceptions: 'generally' (hedged); realization varies by speech style; enclitic /-nyi/ ~ /-yi/ attracts the accent to the preceding syllable (p.88). Kagaya 2000 §5.4 mentions exceptions 'discussed below' to the one-syllable-one-mora rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Explicitly pre-pausal ('next to last syllable before a pause') — phrase/utterance-level penultimate accent that coincides with word-penult in citation forms; Kagaya's statement is for verbs uttered in isolation. Language is tonal; the accent is described as separate from tone.
new_statements.identity_note: Stevick 1965 is titled 'Shona Basic Course' but its Foreword states the material represents 'Manyika varieties of Shona' (informants Mr. and Mrs. Matthew Mataranyika), 'with certain systematic emendations in the direction of the more central dialects' — so it is Manyika-based but lightly standardized toward Zezuru (core1255/shon1251). Kagaya 2000 and Yukawa 1999 describe Zimbabwean Manyika (Yukawa's informant: Mutare-born, Rusape-raised; Yukawa himself notes possible Zezuru influence). Ngunga & Faquir 2011 describe Mozambican Cimanyika (Manica, Barwe). All fall under many1258.

sources.note: Foreword p.iv: course 'based on the speech of two individuals, representing Manyika varieties of Shona'. catalog record Note 1 p.4: 'accent' = extra force of articulation + extra duration, independent of tone; 'generally falls on the next to last syllable before a pause'; in some styles realized as noticeable vowel prolongation. catalog record Note 3 p.88: enclitic /-nyi/ (easterly form) is pronounced with the preceding word, so the syllable before it gets the penultimate accent (Ndiri kuita basa -> /ba/; Uri kuita basanyi -> /sa/).

sources.note: p.154 §5.4 '次末音節の長音化' (lengthening of the penultimate syllable): in modern Manyika, as in modern Zezuru, when a verb is uttered in isolation that syllable is lengthened and appears two morae long; in other positions one syllable = one mora. (The first sentence prints 語末音節 'word-final syllable' where the heading and the rest of the section say 次末音節 'penultimate' — apparent misprint.) No 'stress' terminology; tone treated as H/L.
